questions.answer: It transfers 75 J of energy every second while operating at that power.
questions.unit_policy: No extra unit is required because the selected statement contains joules and seconds.

option_feedback.A: A watt is a rate, not a fixed amount of stored energy.
option_feedback.B: Correct. One watt is one joule per second, so 75 W means 75 J transferred each second.
option_feedback.C: Seventy-five joules per minute would be only 1.25 W, not 75 W.
option_feedback.D: Total energy also depends on operating time, so a lower-power device can transfer more energy if it runs longer.

marking_points.text: Selects option B, identifying 75 W as 75 J transferred per second.

questions.answer: Machine Y has greater power because 450 W is greater than 300 W.
questions.unit_policy: The selected option includes power values in watts.

option_feedback.A: Comparing energy alone ignores the different transfer times. Machine X transfers at 12000/40 = 300 W.
option_feedback.B: A longer time for a given energy reduces power rather than increasing it.
option_feedback.C: Correct. Machine Y transfers at 9000/20 = 450 W, which exceeds Machine X's 300 W.
option_feedback.D: Using the same energy unit does not make the rates equal; each energy must be divided by its own time.

marking_points.text: Selects option C, correctly comparing 450 W with 300 W.
